independence_declaration.statement: I (code-security-reviewer) authored none of the implementation in the reviewed scope (tools/gates, tools/agents, tools/source, .claude/agents, the CI workflow, the analysis and delivery records). I formed this verdict before reading any other round-15 review record, and I read none: I saw only the file names in the round-15 directory. All my code execution ran in disposable clones inside this run's private TMPDIR. The live race probe wrote only to a directory I created for it, which I then removed, and it touched no other agent's files.

checks_run.actual: At start HEAD was 2c24f2e: 2 metadata-only commits after 7fab49c (round-15 assignments, the manifest, stages.json, orchestrator probe evidence). Findings:
- Frontmatter tool lists include no NotebookEdit or MultiEdit, and the matcher covers Write|Edit|NotebookEdit|MultiEdit.
- The CI workflow has contents: read, SHA-pinned actions, fetch-depth 0, and every step fails the job.
- The runner adds a per-run mktemp -d with mode 700, a trap cleanup and exported TMPDIR/MTH_RUN_TMP, plus a stage-validated agent_settings call.
- The node compile cache in MTH_RUN_TMP holds only CLI-start entries (72 at 23:25Z) and none from the ~20 hook invocations, so the hook does not load cached code.
- No new issue beyond F-DG0-145 and F-DG0-146.

summary:
FAIL.

F-DG0-143 and F-DG0-144 are fixed for the mechanisms they describe: both CLOSED_VERIFIED, reproduced on 1e64eb0 and blocked on 7fab49c, and their new tests fail on the old code. Tests pass 76/76 and 17/17, and prefreeze passes 11/11 in a fresh clone. The candidate ID is deterministic across --ref, locales and CRLF checkouts.

New High finding, a mandatory violation. F-DG0-145: the write guard is check-then-use. A symlink that the agent's own sandboxed shell keeps swapping lets a file-tool write pass the hook and land somewhere forbidden. Offline, 236 of 600 attempts did so. Live, with the real Write tool, 1 of 11 did, into a repository directory outside my scope. The most damaging target is another run's private TMPDIR, which re-opens the F-DG0-144 threat for file tools without a trace.

New Low observation, F-DG0-146: transient sandbox stub files perturb the working-tree candidate and --reconcile. This fails closed.
